decisive_items: Acute extensive partially occlusive pulmonary emboli in distal main pulmonary arteries extending into lobar and segmental branches of upper and lower lobes bilaterally
Dilated right ventricle with reduced systolic function, flattened interventricular septum, pulmonary hypertension, and small hyperdynamic left ventricle
An 82-year-old man was hospitalized with several episodes of dizziness, syncope, and shortness of breath
response.rationale: CT angiogram directly demonstrates acute bilateral pulmonary emboli, with clinical features and right heart strain consistent with acute pulmonary embolism. Post-embolic pulmonary hypertension implies a chronic/post-event state not established here.

rejected.why: Post-embolic suggests chronic or prior embolism, whereas the CT shows acute emboli.
Right ventricular dysfunction is a complication of the embolism, not the primary diagnosis.
Cardiac disease is too broad and the prior CAD is not the acute cause.
Cor pulmonale is a secondary right heart consequence of the acute PE, less specific than PE itself.
Colon cancer is historical and only a risk factor, not the acute diagnosis.
Sepsis is unsupported; there is no evidence of infection.
Cardiac ischemia is contradicted by ECG showing no ischemia, and troponin elevation is explained by PE-related strain.
